beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — open on the Claude UI, ask shown answered
beats.narration_text: Ciao — this is Liam, in for Bear. Every Remotion render in this toolkit just started crashing, mid-build, with a cryptic dyld symbol error. Before touching a single beat sheet, I asked Claude what was actually going on.

show.event: composer cold-opens, spark + 'Ciao, Liam' greeting settles
command types itself in: the crash question
send arms, runningText 'diagnosing…' plays
three RESULT lines land in sequence

props.command: Every Remotion render just crashed with a dyld symbol error. What's actually going on?
output: it's not a bug in the beat sheet

beats.role_note: the problem, the context, the stakes — BEFORE the CLI loop
beats.narration_text: Here's the stakes. This whole toolkit's pipeline — every ai-explainer, cli-explainer, deep-explainer reel — ends at the same choke point: a Remotion render. If that render can't run at all, nothing downstream matters — no beat sheet, no audio, no gate discipline fixes a toolchain that won't even start. The question this video answers: was this a bug we wrote, or something underneath our code entirely?

show.event: three reel-type chips fly in from the left, one per spoken kind: ai-explainer, cli-explainer, deep-explainer
all three arcs converge on the single render step on the right
settle line lands: 'no render, nothing downstream'

beats.narration_text: The ask: read the actual crash. 'Symbol not found: underscore-A-V-Capture-Device-Type-Continuity-Camera,' inside libavdevice dot dylib, built for macOS fifteen, referenced from AVFoundation. What do I check first?

show.event: composer already shows the typed command (no typing animation — inner beat)
runningText 'probing the binary…' plays

props.command: Symbol not found: _AVCaptureDeviceTypeContinuityCamera in libavdevice.dylib, built for macOS 15.0, referenced from AVFoundation. What do I check first?

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL command run this session, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it before trusting it. One tool, otool, reads the binary's own load commands. The line that matters is minos — the minimum OS the binary was built for. This copy says fifteen. This Mac is thirteen point four. That gap is the whole crash, before a single frame renders.

show.event: code card fades in
the 'minos 15.0' line highlights on the spoken word

props.title: probe-minos.sh
props.code:
otool -l node_modules/@remotion/compositor-darwin-arm64/libavdevice.dylib \
  | grep -A3 LC_BUILD_VERSION

#       cmd LC_BUILD_VERSION
#  platform 1
#     minos 15.0      <- this Mac is macOS 13.4

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot -> Remotion rhetorical pattern (BinaryBranch)
beats.narration_text: Two ways this could go. Our beat sheet, malformed — fixable in a text editor. Or the binary itself, compiled for an OS newer than this machine — fixable only by changing what's installed. The otool output resolves it: dyld aborts at process start, loading the library, before our code runs at all. Not our bug.

show.event: question card settles, two branch paths draw on
outcome cards land: 'our code' vs 'the binary'
resolver bar lands: 'it's the binary'

data.question: Bug in the beat sheet, or something lower?

resolver.label: It's the binary
resolver.detail: dyld aborts before a single frame renders

data.ghostText: the crash happens at process start, not at render time

beats.narration_text: That's a version problem, not a code problem. The fix: stop assuming the newest package is the right one. Iterate — find the newest compositor build that still targets macOS thirteen, not fifteen.

show.event: composer already shows the typed revision command
runningText 'sweeping versions…' plays

props.command: Find the newest @remotion/compositor-darwin-arm64 version that still targets macOS 13, not 15.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL sweep script run this session
beats.narration_text: A binary search, literally. Pull each version's package, probe the same minos line. Four-three-one through four-three-eight all say thirteen. Four-three-nine flips to fifteen. One patch version is the entire boundary.

show.event: code card fades in
the '4.0.438 -> 13.0' / '4.0.439 -> 15.0' lines highlight on the spoken numbers

props.title: probe-versions.sh
props.code:
for v in 431 433 435 436 437 438 439; do
  npm pack "@remotion/compositor-darwin-arm64@4.0.$v"
  tar -xzf remotion-compositor-darwin-arm64-4.0.$v.tgz
  otool -l package/libavdevice.dylib | grep -A3 LC_BUILD_VERSION | grep minos
done

# 4.0.431 -> 13.0
# 4.0.437 -> 13.0
# 4.0.438 -> 13.0   <- last good
# 4.0.439 -> 15.0   <- the bump

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot -> Remotion rhetorical pattern (DivergentFates)
beats.narration_text: Same package, one version apart, two different fates. Four-three-eight runs clean on this Mac. Four-three-nine — nothing else changed — SIGABRTs at the same load command. Pin to four-three-eight, reinstall, and every render that failed an hour ago just works.

show.event: 'compositor-darwin-arm64' sits at the split point
two tracks diverge: 4.0.438 arcs up good, 4.0.439 arcs down warn
endpoint badges land: 'runs clean' vs 'SIGABRT'

beats.narration_text: So the crash was never a beat sheet bug, and it was never really 'Remotion is broken.' It was one dependency pin, one patch version past the last one built for this OS. The fix wasn't cleverer code — it was reading the binary's own version stamp before touching a single prop.

show.event: three artifact lines stagger in, one per spoken claim

artifactLines: Not a beat-sheet bug, and not "Remotion is broken" — one dependency pin, one patch version past the last one built for this OS.
4.0.438 → minos 13.0, runs clean. 4.0.439 → minos 15.0, SIGABRTs on this Mac. Nothing else changed.
The fix wasn't cleverer code — it was reading the binary's own LC_BUILD_VERSION before touching a single prop.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, viewer-addressed
beats.narration_text: Your turn — here's the prompt, read it with me. 'My compiled dependency crashes with a dyld Symbol not found error on my OS version. Show me how to check the binary's LC_BUILD_VERSION with otool, then find the newest package version that still targets my OS.' Run it before you assume the newest version is the right one. Liam, in for Bear.
